# QS-CFW-5998-73 - Quality specification - track link CFW-5998-73 (15B37)
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5998-73

Scope
This quality specification governs the manufacturing acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for forged track links supplied under the part identifier CFW-5998-73. It applies to all process steps performed at Plant P2 for the referenced part and to any subcontracted forging operations that will deliver product to Plant P2 for final machining and assembly. The intent is to control material and process outputs that affect fit, function, and service life of the track link.

Background and rationale
Track link performance in service is governed by hardness, dimensional accuracy of critical features, and mass control during forging. Hardness affects wear and fatigue resistance of the mating surface. Bore geometry governs fitment on the pivot pin and directly impacts assembly clearance and kinematics. Controlling forging mass ensures consistent upset and grain flow for downstream heat treatment and machining. The requirements below are set to balance field durability and manufacturability based on engineering evaluations and service feedback.

Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance note |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness | The hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 34-38 HRC. | Hardness shall be measured after final heat treatment and prior to any machining that would alter the surface hardness. Localized grinding that removes material from the test surface is not permitted before hardness verification. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is ±0.10 mm. | Applies to the finished bore after any machining operations. Concentricity and roundness shall be controlled to ensure the tolerance is meaningful for assembly; when bore is at tolerance limit, mating pin fit must be confirmed by assembly trial records. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73) is 4.8 kg. | Weight must be recorded on the heat/lot traceability record. Forgings exceeding this mass may have altered material flow and shall not be released without engineering disposition. |

Inspection method
Material traceability and initial verification
- Verify incoming material certification is present for each heat lot and reconcile to the lot/heat number captured in production records. Confirm chemical and mechanical properties meet the base material specification recorded for CFW-5998-73.

Hardness verification
- Hardness testing shall be performed on representative locations defined for the part family and recorded in the inspection record. Test locations shall be selected from non-machined surfaces that represent the worst-case case for hardness after heat treatment. Use a calibrated hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale. Record individual test readings and the test location identifiers on the inspection form. Acceptance is per the hardness range stated in the requirements table. If a reading falls outside the range, tag the part as nonconforming and proceed per the nonconformance handling section.

Bore dimensional inspection
- Inspect the finished bore using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement to verify the bore diameter is within the bore diameter tolerance specified in the requirements table. Record the measured values and the measuring instrument identifier on the inspection form. For production runs where a first-piece inspection is required, retain the first-piece report in the part lot file. If bore inspection shows deviation, stop release of the lot and follow the nonconformance handling procedure.

Forging mass control
- Weigh each forging after trimming and before heat treatment; record the mass on the heat/lot traceability record. Ensure the measured mass does not exceed the maximum forging weight specified in the requirements table. If the mass exceeds the stated maximum, segregate the forging and notify engineering for disposition.

Sampling and acceptance rationale
- The inspection plan focuses on attributes that most affect assembly fit and service life. Hardness is controlled to maintain fatigue and wear resistance. Bore tolerance is controlled to ensure functional fit and to prevent accelerated wear or misalignment. Forging mass is limited to maintain consistent metallurgical properties and prevent process anomalies. Records from each inspection activity are retained to support traceability and to provide data for continuous improvement.

Examples of acceptable and non-acceptable conditions
- Acceptable: Part with recorded hardness readings within the specified hardness range for track link CFW-5998-73 (CFW-5998-73), bore measurements all within the stated bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm, and recorded mass at or below the maximum forging weight 4.8 kg.
- Non-acceptable: Part with hardness readings outside 34-38 HRC; part with any bore measurement outside ±0.10 mm of nominal; forging with recorded mass greater than 4.8 kg.

Records to keep
- Heat/lot traceability record including incoming material certification and forging mass for each part.
- Hardness test records including instrument calibration identifier, test locations, and individual readings.
- Bore inspection records including measurement device identifier and raw measured values.
- Disposition records and nonconformance reports for any part that fails the stated requirements.
- Retain records per Plant P2 document retention policy and make available for internal audit and customer inquiries.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
- Any part found outside the limits stated in the requirements table shall be tagged as nonconforming and physically segregated from conforming inventory. Marking shall include the part identifier CFW-5998-73 and the reason for nonconformance.

Containment and notification
- Immediately notify production supervision and quality engineering. Capture the nonconformance on the official nonconformance report and attach the inspection records that triggered the report.

Evaluation and disposition
- Quality engineering and manufacturing engineering shall evaluate the cause and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include repair where feasible, rework under an approved procedure, scrap, or engineering review for use-as-is with customer approval. Any repair or rework proposal must include steps to ensure the repaired part will meet the requirements in the table and must be approved in writing by engineering.

Corrective action and records
- Root cause analysis shall be conducted for nonconformances that indicate a systemic issue. Implement corrective actions and document effectiveness. All disposition and corrective action records shall be filed with the lot records for the affected parts and made available for audits.

Revision control
- Changes to this specification require documented approval by quality engineering at Plant P2 and shall be recorded in the revision history.
